To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new technique that enables the patterning of large-area arrays of holes smaller than 50 nm with a high aspect ratio and that we have demonstrated the selective area growth on these substrates of high quality GaAs NWs with a high vertical density.

we have shown that the surface preparation of the Si substrate is crucial for selective area growth of NWs and that we have demonstrated the applicability of nano imprint lithography in combination with indirect pattern transfer for the fabrication of large arrays of GaAs NWs on Si(111).
we have demonstrated the successful growth of GaAs NWs on Si(111), which is a key step towards the realization of III-V on Si nanophotonic devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique that enables the patterning of large areas with nanoscale resolution, which is a prerequisite for the fabrication of NW based devices.
the selective area growth by Ga-assisted MBE on Si(111), which is a crucial step for the realization of III-V/Si heterostructures.
the development of new methods to pattern substrates for the growth of NWs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the vertical yield of Ga-assisted selective area growth of NWs on Si(111), which is the most challenging substrate for this technique, is improved by reducing the atomic roughness in the mask openings.
the combination of the two patterning techniques, EBL and NIL-IPT, enables the selective growth of GaAs NWs with a high vertical density on Si substrates.
the surface preparation by boiling the substrate in water is a crucial step to achieve a high vertical yield of NW growth on Si(111).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of a surface preparation by boiling in ultra-pure water with a NIL-IPT technique enables the selective area growth on Si(111), with a vertical yield of 80%, of GaAs NWs with a diameter of 30 nm and a length of 1.5 μm.
the combination of the water boiling process and NIL-IPT is the best approach for the growth of GaAs NWs on Si(111), which is of interest for the realization of NW-based electronic devices.
the surface preparation of the substrate is crucial for the growth of high vertical yield Ga-assisted GaAS NWs on Si(111).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface preparation of the substrate has a significant impact on the growth of GaAs NWs on Si(111).
the vertical NW growth yield can be improved by reducing atomic roughness on the Si surface in the mask opening.
the surface preparation prior to the growth of Ga-assist GaAs NWs on Si(111)-patterned substrates has a major impact on the vertical yield of the NWs.
